messages.content: Hi everyone! I'm about to play a new character for the first time, and I'm hoping to get community help to make sure I built this correctly. [The character's sheet is here](https://zeshanrajput.github.io/sr6velvet/chapters/character_sheet.html), or [the XML is on GitHub](https://github.com/zeshanrajput/sr6velvet/blob/main/input/Velvet.xml). I'll put my specific questions in a 🧵. Thank you!!

2) I took the adept power for astral perception because I think mystic adepts have to in order to be able to perceive astral. a) Is that true? b) Are there other ways to perceive astral that are more cost effective?
3) It wasn't an option in CommLink but I *think* it should be legal - can you take the adept power 'improved ability' for sorcery?
4) I was following a comment MedTec made about a commlink being able to get DR 7 using a securelink, but securelink is limited to the base firewall of the device? Am I missing something?
A) yes it is, if you are not using life path system
B) no specific needed all metas can be surge, except if life path is used

4) commlink is 3/1 but with changing attributes it can be set to 1/3 which then allows to boost the fw by another 3 due tto securelink

(For now, I kept quickening as this character's 'Veteran Mode' button.)

next up is to try STT and see what the build looks like. My priorities (and order of priority) remain roughly the same for this experiment:
* don't do anything SRM illegal
* design a viable social mysad for normal play without quickening (12-15ish pools for influence, sorcery)
* get to CHA 10 if possible
* have an option for veteran play
* have 2-3 interesting ways to re-leverage CHA in combat

So I had time to get back to these experiments, specifically comparing Sum-to-Ten to Life Path through the lens of this use case. For my experiments, I went with A Attributes, B Magic, and D Meta, Skills, and Resources. 
* Attributes: I ended with 4 fewer attributes and 1 fewer edge via STT. This is actually very comparable given that a) I prioritized attributes in both build designs, and b) a Dalek gets +4 attributes from racial maximums during 'Born This Way'. 
* Skills: 16 in STT vs 17 in Life Path. Again, I thought this was very comparable. I do appreciate that Life Path 'forced' a more well rounded character, while STT gave me the opportunity to get specializations in the character's areas of focus.
* Resources were identical in both
* Meta allowed the desired MAG 6, but the Edge in STT (2) is slightly lower than Life Path (3). 

Karma
- Not having the option (AFAIK) to spend 30 karma to increase starting PP was a good deal of personal reflection for me. The 30 karma that LP can spend here is within 6 karma of any character spending their first three submersions on PP (and potentially less if you have access to a Coven). Now, I know that submersions are a fininte long term resource, but again I was struck by how comparable this was.
- Not having the option also forced me to re-evaluate many other aspects of my goals. Several of these have already been pointed out above, such as the real value proposition of commanding voice and sharp tongue for a mysad with access to stunbolt, etc. So personal learning, but I don't think worthy of report.

Conclusion - I was shocked to find STT so comparable. It's undeniable that LP had a net stronger value (in this n-of-1 unoptimized experiment, some napkin math came out to 20 karma difference given that the move from CHA 9 --> 10 would be 50) but the effect at the table is actually only 1-2 dice in secondary pools.

Just to wrap this thread up, some final learnings:

* I was able to leverage the same python infrastructure I used for life path to fix the original point buy build. Doing so yielded a character that was within 5 karma of STT.
* I ended up going with Life Path because the design decisions forced a more well-rounded and interesting character to play. I would absolutely build a character with Life Path again and use it to seed my thoughts on background narrative. 
* I was really pleased at how balanced the three generation systems were given how disparate their rules are! If better balance were desired I might suggest removing the increase in attributes when the maximum is higher than 6, and the ability for anyone to buy power points. Other than that, I really do think the differences were pretty appropriate to the strength and weakness each build had. 

One other learning that I'm not entirely sure what to do with yet - I have reservations about how I built Yuriko now (I used point buy in CommLink6 for her too). I'm not confident that her points were calculated correctly either. I'll try to rebuild her initial build tomorrow, but i'm hoping I don't find anything.

And the final note is a TREMENDOUS THANKS to all of you for having the patience to teach me over the past few days. I feel so much more confident with each of these systems now, and much better calibrated on the range of characters I could and should expect to join my tables. Thank you!!

[This is actually pretty easy to model.](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1Ta6vMd3zru07BR0gT84nUCuEn51LcshVM95vPntEOUc/edit?usp=sharing) Based on this, you'd spend 81 karma without a coven. Each increase in reputation saves you [# of total initiations] in karma, with 5+ costing you a major downtime instead of a minor every two SRMs (in other words, slowing your potential initiation velocity in half).

But there's a cost in time to accumulate the karma. If you alternate CMPs with SRMs then you can 'keep up' with the cost escalation scale at loyalty 4. But if you play back to back SRMs, loyalty 8 means you net total karma but your rate of progression is still the same (one every two missions) as loyalty 4. This ultimately frees karma and forces non-initiation forms of progression.
